title: Book: Rich Dad Poor Dad — Robert Kiyosaki (1997)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Robert Kiyosaki contrasts two 'dads' — his father (a salaried professional) and his friend's father (an entrepreneur-investor) — to argue that financial education is not taught in school and that the rich build assets instead of working only for a salary. His headline idea: an asset puts money into your pocket and a liability takes money out, so focus on buying assets (businesses, investments, income-producing property) rather than consumption that looks like wealth. Other themes: don't work only for money, learn how taxes and companies work, and overcome fear and laziness. Criticisms to keep in mind: the two-dads story is widely questioned as a parable rather than fact; 'your home is not an asset' is a simplification; the book gives little concrete, safe guidance and promotes leverage and real estate, which carry real risk; and the author sells related products. Use it for motivation, not as a financial plan.
